newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EMERSON GIVEN WARNING BY MIDDLESBROUGH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EMERSON GIVEN WARNING BY MIDDLESBROUGH.

text.p: Middlesbrough chairman Steve Gibson has warned his wayward Brazilian star Emerson he will not be allowed to leave the club.
The player will be told to honour his contract when he returns from his latest trip to Brazil, despite his wife's apparent reluctance to live in England.
"The club's position is clear. Emerson cannot be allowed to leave," said Gibson.
"It would send out the wrong signals right across football if Middlesbrough can be dictated to and bullied. We are not prepared to sacrifice our reputation by allowing this to happen.
"Emerson has brought ill repute to the town with all these alleged comments coming from himself and his wife.
"To date Emerson has been fined six weeks' salary and we will continue to fine him the maximum amount until he conforms."
Gibson also criticised agents for their part in unsettling Emerson and laid part of the blame with Spanish giants Barcelona, who have been strongly linked with the Brazilian.

"We are disappointed by Emerson but we believe he has been badly advised," he added. "There has been a disgraceful manipulation of the player so that somebody can profit from the sale of Emerson to Barcelona.
"I must add that Barcelona's conduct in this affair requires investigation.
"The events of this past month have been carefully orchestrated by Emerson's agent with a possible remit by Barcelona."
Emerson is believed to earn about 8,000 pounds per week basic salary which means he has already paid around 50,000 pounds in club fines.
He signed a four-year contract this year, but has not yet informed the club when he intends to return from Brazil where his wife Andrea is reportedly ill.
"Emerson is contracted to us until June 2000. We want him to spend the best years of his career with us, hopefully win caps for Brazil as well and possibly play in the next World Cup.
"So he is staying here. If he doesn't comply he will lose everything and it will cost him his career."
